rate_description: No tax at grant. India taxes the ESOP perquisite at allotment of shares (i.e., exercise), not at grant.
filing_requirement: No filing at grant. Employer records the grant for later Form 12BA / Form 16 reporting.

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — perquisite arises on allotment / transfer of shares to the employee
citations.note: The perquisite is triggered when the share is allotted to the employee, which (in ESOP structures) is at exercise — not at grant or vest.

rate_description: No tax at vest. Vesting alone does not allot a share; the option is still unexercised.

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) read with Rule 3(8) — taxable event is allotment, not vesting

rate_description: Perquisite value = (FMV on date of exercise − exercise price) × number of options exercised. Taxed as 'Salaries' at the employee's applicable slab rate (currently up to 30% plus surcharge and 4% cess).
withholding_note: Employer must deduct TDS under Section 192 (Income-tax Act 1961) / Section 392(1) (Income-tax Act 2025) at the average rate of income-tax for the year on the perquisite value.
filing_requirement: Employer Form 12BA (annexure to Form 16, by 15 June following FY) and Form 16 (annual). Employee reports in ITR-2 / ITR-3.
documents_required: Merchant banker valuation report (unlisted) or NSE/BSE price evidence (listed)

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — perquisite from allotment of specified security or sweat equity share
Rule 3(8) — FMV computation. Listed: average of opening and closing market prices on exercise date. Unlisted: SEBI Category-I merchant banker valuation, valid for up to 180 days from valuation date.
Section 192 — TDS on salary at average rate
Section 17(5)(h) — successor to ITA 1961 §17(2)(vi) for FMV-based perquisite valuation
citations.note: ITA 2025 renumbers but does not substantively change the ESOP perquisite rule.

caveats: Employees of DPIIT-recognized eligible startups may defer TDS under §192(1C) (ITA 1961) — TDS becomes payable at the earliest of: (a) 48 months after end of relevant AY, (b) date of sale, (c) date of cessation of employment.
If FMV is not determined per Rule 3(8) (e.g., stale merchant banker valuation), the perquisite computation is open to challenge by the Assessing Officer.
Surcharge: 10% if income > ₹50L, 15% > ₹1Cr, 25% > ₹2Cr, 37% > ₹5Cr (capped at 25% under the new regime). Health & education cess: 4%.

rate_description: Capital gain = sale consideration − FMV on exercise date (cost basis already taxed as perquisite). Listed shares: STCG (held ≤12 months) at 20% under §111A; LTCG (>12 months) on gain >₹1.25L at 12.5% under §112A (post-Budget 2024 rates). Unlisted shares: STCG (≤24 months) at slab; LTCG (>24 months) at 12.5% without indexation.
withholding_note: No TDS on resident-to-resident share sales as a default; TCS may apply only in specific listed-exchange contexts.
filing_requirement: Employee reports gains in ITR-2 (Schedule CG). Pays advance tax in quarterly instalments if total annual tax > ₹10,000.

citations.reference: Section 111A — STCG on listed equity (rate raised from 15% to 20% w.e.f. 23 July 2024)
Section 112A — LTCG on listed equity exceeding ₹1.25 lakh (rate revised to 12.5% w.e.f. 23 July 2024)
Section 112 — LTCG on unlisted shares at 12.5% (Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 removed indexation benefit)
Section 48 — cost of acquisition for ESOP shares = FMV used for perquisite taxation

caveats: Cost basis for the share = the FMV that was used to compute the perquisite at exercise — not the original exercise price. Double-counting is avoided this way.
Holding-period clock starts from the allotment date (exercise), not the grant date.
Pre-23 July 2024 sales used the old rates (STCG 15%, LTCG 10% on listed; 20% with indexation on unlisted). Verify sale date against rate-change cut-off.

rate_description: No Indian tax at grant. The parent's jurisdiction does not alter the Indian rule — perquisite arises at allotment (exercise), not at grant.
filing_requirement: Indian employer (subsidiary) records the grant for later Form 12BA / Form 16 reporting.

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — perquisite arises on allotment of shares, regardless of which group entity grants the option

caveats: The Indian subsidiary is the 'employer' for TDS purposes even when the option is granted by the overseas parent — cross-charge under transfer pricing arrangements is standard.

rate_description: No Indian tax at vest. Vesting is not an allotment.

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) read with Rule 3(8)

caveats: Assumes the employee renders zero services in the parent's jurisdiction during the vesting and pre-event period. Any partial-period workdays in that jurisdiction can attach a source-tax claim under its territorial-nexus rules; re-run with apportionment if material.

rate_description: Indian perquisite tax applies in full. Perquisite value = (FMV on exercise date − exercise price) × options exercised. Slab-rate tax (up to 30% + surcharge + 4% cess). TDS by the Indian subsidiary as the employer-of-record.
withholding_note: Indian subsidiary, not the SG parent, deducts TDS under §192. The subsidiary typically funds this via cash recovery from the employee or via parent cross-charge.
filing_requirement: Indian subsidiary issues Form 12BA + Form 16. Employee files ITR-2/ITR-3. SG parent has no Indian filing obligation directly.
documents_required: SEBI Cat-I merchant banker valuation (for unlisted SG parent shares)
Cross-charge invoice from SG parent (transfer-pricing trail)

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — perquisite from specified-security allotment by any employer (including foreign parent)
Rule 3(8) — FMV: SEBI Cat-I merchant banker valuation for unlisted shares (SG parent's unlisted equity falls here)
Section 192 — TDS by Indian employer (subsidiary)

caveats: FEMA: forex remittance for exercise-price payment routed via LRS (US$ 250k annual cap per RBI). If exercise is cashless (parent issues shares net of price), LRS is not engaged.
Transfer pricing: SG parent must invoice Indian subsidiary for the perquisite cost (cross-charge) at arm's length, supported by valuation evidence.
DPIIT-recognized eligible startup deferral (§192(1C)) applies only if the *Indian subsidiary* itself is the DPIIT-recognized startup — not the SG parent.

rate_description: Indian capital gains apply on sale of the SG parent's shares by the India-resident employee. Holding period > 24 months: LTCG at 12.5% (without indexation post-2024). ≤24 months: STCG at slab rate.
filing_requirement: Employee reports in ITR-2 Schedule CG. Pays advance tax quarterly.
documents_required: Foreign asset disclosure in ITR Schedule FA

citations.reference: Section 112 — LTCG on unlisted shares at 12.5% (Finance (No. 2) Act 2024)
Section 48 — cost basis = FMV used for perquisite (no double tax)
Schedule FA — disclosure of foreign assets and income, mandatory for India-resident holders of SG parent shares

caveats: Singapore-India DTAA: Article 13 governs capital gains. For unlisted-share sales, the source-country rule typically allows India to tax India-resident sellers — confirm with the latest protocol.
Schedule FA non-disclosure carries severe penalties under the Black Money Act 2015 — flag this explicitly for the employee.

rate_description: No Indian tax on exercise gain for an SG-resident, non-Indian-source employee. Salary income is sourced where services are rendered; services rendered in Singapore are not Indian source.

citations.reference: Section 5 read with Section 9(1)(ii) — non-resident income is taxable only if earned for services rendered in India
Article 15 — Dependent Personal Services. Salary is taxable only in the country of employment exercise (Singapore in this case).

caveats: If the employee was India-resident at any point between grant and exercise, partial-period apportionment can attach Indian tax — re-run with that scenario.
OCI status, prior India tax residency, or any India workday count during the vesting window may shift the analysis. Confirm employee's residency profile.

rate_description: No Indian tax on the sale gain for a non-resident, non-Indian-source employee. India would only tax the gain if the shares qualify as Indian-source assets — which IN-parent unlisted shares typically do.
withholding_note: However, see caveat: §195 TDS by the BUYER may apply if the IN parent's shares are 'situated in India' (typically yes for unlisted Indian-company shares).
filing_requirement: Non-resident files ITR-2 to claim DTAA relief if Indian tax is withheld at source.

citations.reference: Section 9(1)(i) — capital gain on transfer of an asset situated in India is Indian-source income, taxable on non-residents
Article 13(4) — capital gains on shares of an Indian company by an SG-resident are taxable in India (sourced where the shares are situated).
Section 195 — TDS on payments to non-residents by the buyer

caveats: Confidence is 'conditional' because the result depends on whether the IN-parent's shares are characterized as 'Indian-source' assets — for an unlisted Indian company this is typically yes, triggering Indian capital gains tax at 12.5% LTCG / slab STCG even on non-resident sellers.
DTAA Article 13(4) was amended in 2017 — capital gains on Indian-company shares acquired by SG residents AFTER 1 April 2017 lost the SG-exemption benefit. Confirm acquisition date.
Pure compliance-engine output; transfer-pricing and treaty positions require counsel.

rate_description: Indian perquisite tax applies in full when an India-resident employee exercises options granted by a UK parent. Perquisite value = (FMV at exercise − exercise price) × options exercised. Slab-rate tax up to 30% + surcharge + 4% cess. The Indian subsidiary is the employer-of-record and TDS withholder under §192 / ITA 2025 §392(1).
withholding_note: Indian subsidiary withholds; cross-charge from UK parent via inter-company invoice at arm's length.
filing_requirement: Form 12BA + Form 16 by Indian subsidiary; employee files ITR-2/ITR-3.
documents_required: SEBI Cat-I merchant banker valuation (UK unlisted shares)

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — perquisite from specified-security allotment, applies regardless of foreign parent's jurisdiction
Rule 3(8) — FMV via SEBI Cat-I merchant banker for unlisted UK parent shares
Article 16 — Dependent Personal Services. Primary taxing right India for IN-resident performing services in IN.

caveats: FEMA / LRS applies to exercise-price remittance to UK parent — US$250K annual LRS cap. Cashless exercise avoids LRS.
Transfer pricing: UK parent must invoice Indian subsidiary at arm's length.
DPIIT-startup §192(1C) deferral applies only if the *Indian subsidiary* is the DPIIT-recognized startup, not the UK parent.

rate_description: No Indian tax on the exercise gain for a UK-resident, non-Indian-source employee. Salary income is sourced to where services are performed (UK in this case). India-UK DTAA Article 16 confirms primary taxing right rests with the UK.

citations.reference: Section 5 read with Section 9(1)(ii) — non-resident income taxable in India only if earned for services in India
Article 16 — Dependent Personal Services: primary taxing right rests with country of services (UK).

caveats: Assumes zero services rendered in India during vesting and pre-exercise period.
OCI status, prior India residency, or India-workday counts can shift the analysis. Verify employee profile.

rate_description: India perquisite tax on the share option gain. For an Indian-resident engineer employed by the Indian subsidiary of a Hong Kong parent, the gain = (FMV at exercise − exercise price) × shares is a 'perquisite' under §17(2)(vi) of the Income-tax Act 1961, taxed at the employee's slab rate (up to 30% + cess). The Indian employer must withhold TDS under §192 on this notional benefit.
withholding_note: Indian subsidiary deducts TDS under §192 on the perquisite value at the time of exercise; the employer issues Form 12BA and Form 16 reflecting the perquisite.
filing_requirement: Indian employer: Form 12BA (annual statement of perquisites) + Form 16 (annual TDS certificate) + Form 24Q (quarterly TDS return). Employee: ITR-2 / ITR-3 with Schedule FA disclosure of the foreign HK-parent shares.
documents_required: FMV valuation report (Rule 3(8) — Category I Merchant Banker for unlisted)

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — value of any specified security or sweat equity shares allotted or transferred to an employee is a perquisite
Rule 3(8) — FMV determination for unlisted securities by Category I Merchant Banker on the exercise date
Section 192 — TDS on salary including perquisite value of ESOP exercise
India–Hong Kong Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, Article 14 — Income from Employment; Article 23 — Methods for Elimination of Double Taxation (credit method)

caveats: If any portion of the vesting period involved services in HK (HK workdays > 60 in a year of assessment), a secondary HK Salaries Tax charge may arise — claim foreign tax credit on the IN return under India–HK CDTA Article 23.

Eligible-startup deferral under §192(1C): if the Indian employer is a DPIIT-recognized eligible startup, TDS on the perquisite can be deferred to the earliest of: 48 months from end of relevant assessment year, employee ceasing employment, or sale of shares. This rule assumes the standard case (no deferral).

rate_description: No India income tax on the exercise gain. A Hong Kong-resident employee with no Indian employment and no Indian-source services has no Indian tax nexus. §5(2) of the ITA 1961 limits non-resident taxation to income received in India, accruing in India, or deemed to accrue in India under §9. Services rendered wholly outside India do not give rise to deemed-accrual under §9(1)(ii).
filing_requirement: No Indian filing for the HK-resident employee. The Indian parent has internal accounting (Ind AS 102) but no TDS obligation under §192 because no salary is paid by an Indian employer.

citations.reference: Section 5(2) — scope of total income of a non-resident: only income received in India, accruing in India, or deemed to accrue in India
Section 9(1)(ii) — salary income is deemed to accrue in India only if earned in India; services rendered outside India are not in scope
Article 14 (Income from Employment) — employment income is taxable only in the residence state unless services are exercised in the source state

caveats: If the HK-resident employee renders services in India during the vesting period, that proportion of the gain becomes Indian-sourced and chargeable to Indian tax under §9(1)(ii). Confirm Indian workday log.
On subsequent sale of the IN-parent shares, capital gains tax may arise in India under §9(1)(i) (shares of an Indian company are deemed to be situated in India).

rate_description: India perquisite tax on the share option gain. For an Indian-resident employee of an Indian subsidiary of a UAE parent, the gain = (FMV at exercise − exercise price) × shares is a perquisite under §17(2)(vi) of the Income-tax Act 1961, taxed at the employee's slab rate (up to 30% + cess). TDS under §192 by the Indian employer.
withholding_note: Indian subsidiary deducts TDS under §192 on the perquisite value at exercise.
filing_requirement: Indian employer: Form 12BA + Form 16 + Form 24Q. Employee: ITR-2 / ITR-3 with Schedule FA disclosure of foreign UAE-parent shares.

citations.reference: Section 17(2)(vi) — value of specified security / sweat equity shares allotted is a perquisite
Rule 3(8) — FMV determination for unlisted securities by Category I Merchant Banker
Section 192 — TDS on salary including perquisite value of ESOP exercise
Article 15 (Dependent Personal Services) — employment income taxable in state where services exercised (India); Article 25 — Methods for elimination of double taxation

caveats: UAE has no personal income tax — no foreign tax credit issue arises on the IN side because there is no UAE tax to credit against.
Eligible-startup deferral under §192(1C): if the Indian employer is DPIIT-recognized, TDS deferral applies. This rule assumes the standard case.

rate_description: No India income tax for a UAE-resident employee with no Indian-source services during the vesting period. §5(2) limits non-resident taxation to income received / accruing / deemed-accruing in India. Services rendered wholly in the UAE are not deemed to accrue in India under §9(1)(ii). The Indian parent has IFRS / Ind AS 102 stock-based compensation accounting, but no TDS obligation under §192 because no Indian salary is paid.
filing_requirement: No Indian filing for the UAE-resident employee. The Indian parent has internal accounting but no TDS/payroll obligation.

citations.reference: Section 5(2) — scope of total income of a non-resident: income received, accruing, or deemed to accrue in India only
Section 9(1)(ii) — salary income is deemed to accrue in India only if earned in India; services rendered outside India are out of scope
Article 15 (Dependent Personal Services) — employment income taxable in state where services exercised

caveats: If any portion of the vesting period involved services in India, that proportion of the gain is Indian-sourced and chargeable in India under §9(1)(ii). Verify Indian workday log — most Indian founders moving to UAE retain some India workdays in the early relocation period.

Confidence is CONDITIONAL because Indian-residency reclassification under §6 (183-day test or 60-day test for Indian citizens) is fact-specific. If the employee remains Indian-tax-resident in the year of exercise, the gain is taxed in India on worldwide-income basis under §5(1).
On subsequent sale of Indian-parent shares, capital gains arise in India under §9(1)(i) (Indian-company shares deemed situated in India), irrespective of the seller's residence.
